Connect is the infotelematic system fitted to this vehicle. It interacts with the user to facilitate driving and make life inside the passenger compartment as pleasant as possible.

The Connect system is not fitted to the vehicle as standard but is available as an option.

Protection against overheating

Telematic system components come with protection against overheating. This cuts off operation when module temperature exceeds a set limit.

In this case, the function activated by the module that has reached the temperature limit is deactivated and a warning message appears on the display.

The user must wait for module temperature to drop below this limit before resuming the interrupted function. This is indicated by the message disappearing from the display followed by function reactivation.

Otherwise, press the ESC key to exit from the screen with the message immediately and activate a different function.

Possible CONNECT statuses from the viewpoint of power supply and operation in general are as follows: OFF Status, Normal Status, StandBy Status

Power supply management

The system may be in one of the following conditions:

  • OFF status with all functions disabled;
  • NORMAL status with all functions active or activatable;
  • STAND-BY status, with functions partially active and screen dark.

OFF status

All Connect functions are disabled and the various hardware modules are not supplied with power.

NORMAL status

The Connect system is fully active and all system functions are managed in accordance with the system configuration.

Internal modules are operational, as are the internal communication lines.

The system configuration is stored when this status is left. It is then restored when the status is resumed.

STAND-BY status

While in this mode, the Connect system is partly active but looks exactly as though it were OFF to the user.

Network localisation and management modules remain active at internal module level.

The following modules are deactivated: Telephone, Radio, Audio, Audio CD and CDC, Voice Recognition, Voice synthesis and Navigation system.

The electrical statuses described earlier are determined by the following actions:

  • activation
  • deactivation
  • stand-by.

Ignition

The system is activated automatically when the ignition key is turned to MAR. When the system is turned on, the status active prior to the last deactivation (normal or stand-by) is restored

When the ignition key is turned to OFF or removed, the system can be turned on by pressing the encode ON/OFF R1 (See Fig. 2), or the Connect key (enter the PIN code to use the phone).

Deactivation

If the system is on (NORMAL or STAND-BY status), it may be turned off by removing the ignition key.

The Connect unit stores the system configuration in its memory when it is turned off.

Deactivation is delayed if a phone call or emergency call is in progress or if the system is changing the voice command language. In this case, the Connect unit turns itself automatically when the call is terminated by the user (if the call lasts longer than 20 minutes) or 20 minutes after key off (if the call lasts less than 20 minutes).

If the Connect unit is turned on with key off (+Key inactive) via the ON/OFF encoder or Connect key, it can be turned off by pressing the ON/OFF encoder again. Otherwise it is turned off automatically after 20 minutes to save battery charge.

Stand-by

During operation, the system may be by-passed to stand-by by a long press on the MAIN key. This operating condition corresponds to a dark screen and volume off. The system continues to work in stand-by mode, however, because the phone remains ready to receive.

If the limit of one active function is exceeded during stand-by, an appropirate warning message is displayed.

To restore the system to normal operating mode, press the MAIN key or Connect key briefly for a "Service call" (the PIN code must be entered to use the phone).

Signals

Because this vehicle is not equipped with a CAN network, the main information must be transmitted to Connect by means of direct physical signals.

These signals are:

  • key signal: turns on the Connect unit when the key is turned On
  • Reverse engaged, to identify vehicle direction of motion.
  • Odometer, to calculate the distance travelled by the vehicle.
  • Light control, to modify screen lighting.

"FREQUENCY" FUNCTION

This function allows manual or automatic tuning/storage of radio stations.

If the "TA" (traffic information) or "PTY" function is active during automatic tuning, the tuner looks only for stations that broadcast traffic news or PTY stations.

"TA" FUNCTION

This function enables the radio to receive traffic news transmitted by some FM stations. The message "TP" appears on the display in this case.

To activate/deactivate the TA (Traffic Announcement) function, press the knob repeatedly after selecting the TA/AF function.

TA/AF functions are activated cyclically by short presses on the knob and occur as follows: AF - TA - TA and AF - both functions off - AF ¿etc.

The message "TA" appears on the display when the TA function is activated.

Listening conditions and display messages are as follows:

  • TA and TP: if the radio is tuned to a station broadcasting traffic information and the traffic information function is active
  • TP: if the radio is tuned to a station broadcasting traffic information and the traffic information function is inactive
  • TA: the traffic information function is active but the radio is tuned to a station that does not broadcast traffic information
  • TA and TP not present on display: the radio is tuned to a station that does not broadcast traffic information and the traffic information function is inactive.

With the TA function active, it is possible to:

  • search only for RDS stations that broadcast in FM and are enabled to broadcast traffic information;
  • Receive traffic information even when the CD player is in operation;
  • Receive traffic information at a minimum preset volume even with the radio volume zeroed or the system set to stand-by.
  • when listening a CD, an automatic search is carried out for another station enabled to transmit traffic information
  • when listening to the radio, an acoustic signal is emitted to warn that traffic information can no longer be received; the signal is cut off by tuning to a station that can broadcast information or by deactivating the TA function

Radio stations in some countries do not broadcast traffic information even when the TP function is active (the message "TP" appears on the display).If the radio is operating in AM band, the radio will tune to the last broadcasting station when the FM band is selected. If the selected station does not broadcast traffic information ("TP" message not shown on display), an automatic search begins for a station enabled for traffic news.If the user alters the volume during a traffic news broadcast, the setting is not shown on the display and the new setting will be maintained only for the news in progress.

If the TA function is active and the tuned station is not enabled to provide traffic information or is no longer able to broadcast this information ("TP" not shown on display), once the radio has continued in this condition for about 1 minute: if a CD is being played, an automatic search is carried out for another station enabled to broadcast traffic information; if the radio is being played, an acoustic signal is emitted to warn that it is no longer possible to receive traffic information. This can only be interrupted by tuning to a station enabled to broadcast traffic information or by deactivating the TA function

"AF" FUNCTION

This function enables reception of radio stations in RDS (Radio Data System) mode

When in RDS mode, the radio can work with:

  • AF ON: active search for alternative frequencies;
  • AF OFF: search for alternative frequencies deactivated.

When the broadcasting RDS station signal weakens, two things may happen:

  • In AF ON mode, the RDS system activates an automatic search for optimum frequencies for the selected station and the radio then tunes automatically to the station with the strongest signal broadcasting the same programme. Passengers can therefore continue to listen to the selected station throughout the trip without altering the frequency when the area changes. It must naturally be possible to receive the broadcasting station in the vehicle's current area.
  • In AF OFF mode, the radio does not tune automatically to the strongest station and the station must be searched for manually by means of the tuning keys.

Press the knob repeatedly to activate/deactivate the AF function after selecting the TA/AF function.

TA/AF functions are activated cyclically by short presses on the knob and occur as follows:

  • AF - TA - TA and AF - both functions off - AF ¿etc.
  • The message "AF" appears on the display when the AF function is activated.
  • The message RDS (if available) remains on the display.

LOC/DX FUNCTION

This function is used to alter the senstivity of the autamatic radio station search. When low sensitivity "LOC" is set, only stations with excellent reception are sought; when high sensitivity "DX" is set, all stations are sought. When in an area where many stations are present and you wish to select those with the strongest signal, set low sensitivity "LOC".

To select between low or high tuner sensitivity, press the knob repeatedly after selecting the function "LOC/DX". The sensitivity setting code is shown on the display:

  • LOC = low sensitivity;
  • DX = high sensitivity.

FUNZIONE "PTY"

The PTY (Program Type) is used to give preference to stations that broadcast programmes classified according to PTY type. The radio contains a list of preset Programme Types for selection. Select the PTY function and confirm with the knob to access a PTY programme list. The display will show a list of PTY programmes and the subject of the last broadcasting station (e.g. NEWS). Turn the knob to scroll through the list of PTY programmes. To select a programme type, press the knob after making a selection.

The FM band must be selected before the PTY function can be activated.

If the station does not broadcast in PTY mode, the message "NO-PTY" appears on the display for 5 seconds.

After 2 seconds, the station name or frequency is displayed.

"EON" (Enhanced Other Network) FUNCTION

Circuits active in certain countries group together several stations enabled to broadcast traffic information. In this case, the programmed being broadcast by the current station will be temporarily suspended to receive traffic information (only with TA function active) whenever this is broadcast by one of the stations on the same circuit. When the tuned station belongs to an EON circuit, the display will show the message "EON".

"AUTOSTORE" FUNCTION

This function allows automatic radio station storage.

When this function is active, the radio automatically stores stations with the strongest signal in decreasing order of signal intensity within the tuned frequency band:

  • 6 stations in the FM1, FM2 or FM3 band or
  • 6 stations in the MW band or
  • 6 stations in the LW band.

If the TA (traffic information) function is active, only stations that broadcast traffic information are stored. This function may be acivated even while listening to a CD.

The message "Autostore" will appear on the display during the automatic storage stage. Deactivate the "Autostore" function by pressing the ESC key to interrupt the automatic storage process; the radio will re-tune to the station broadcasting before the funtion was activated.

Station signals that are currently strongest within the selected band are automatically stored on preset keys T4, T5, T6, T7, T8, T9 (see Fig.2) . Once storage is complete, the radio will automatically tune to the first FM1 station corresponding to the frequency stored for preseletion key "1".

Each station will be stored once only, except in the case of regional programmes that could be stored twice under certain circumstances.

Sometimes the Autostore function may not be able to find 6 stations with strong signals. In this case, only the stations found will be stored.

"ST./MONO" FUNCTION

This function allows stereo reception of stations to be activated/deactivated by pressing the knob after selecting the St./Mono function. When stereo reception is activated, the displays shows the message "STEREO", while the message "MONO" appears when it is deactivated.

When the tuned station frequency is weak, it is advisable to activate the "MONO" function to improve listening quality.

  • Stop : playing is suspended and the optical pick up moves to the beginning of the track sequence.
  • Skip : the optical pick up moves directly to the beginning of the track before or after the current track.
  • Scan: select this control to play the first part of all the tracks on the CD.
  • Eject: use to eject the CD.

Navigation function

The navigation system built into the Connect unit helps the driver reach a selected destination by means of visual and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is flexible to use because it allows the driver to call up pre-programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, historical sights, public organisations, fuel stations or Manufacturer's Authorise Serviced Outlets.

The navigation function is available on all Connect configurations except Level 1.

On the available versions, map navigation can be displayed only on Connect level 4, fitted with a 5" TFT display. - A pictogram navigation system is used for other versions, fitted with LCD graphic displays.

The navigation system is fully managed by the telematic system. The only operations required is therefore to replace the navigation CD-ROM to obtain a map of a different area or an up-to-date map.

Vehicle location

The essential information required by the system in order to set navigation routes is the vehicle's position on the world's surface.

The accuracy with which the system calculates the vehicle's position significantly determines the consistency of navigation routes with the earth's topography and road networks.

For this purpose, the system uses a GPS (Global Positioning System) aided by the interaction of certain sensors.

The GPS on the vehicle is equipped with an aerial and a reception module built into the telematic system. This system dynamically processes satellite signals, reversing signals, information from a gyroscope built into the navigation computer and signals from the odometer. These are all integrated with current vehicle position.

Signals from the odometer are used to determine vehicle displacement, the reversing sensor identifies the direction of motion and the gyroscope indicates the vehicle's angular displacement (turns, direction reversals).

The system constantly compares data from the odometer, reversing sensor, GPS aerial and gyroscope in order to compensate automatically for any event that could in some way lead to a false position reading.

The following GPS measurements are used inside the NIT navigation system:

  • Vehicle position estimation (Latitude, Longitude in radiants, Height in metres).
  • Vehicle speed in m/s along the south-north / east-west axes.
  • Estimate of GPS position error.
  • Quality data relating to input signal: (number of satellites, Y/N ratio, 3D point).
  • Time-fix relating to last measurement taken (used to identify the moment to which the measurement refers).

The result obtained is defined as the "Estimated Vehicle Point", since the vehicle's recorded position diverges from its true position on the ground.

This divergence is due to approximation of the GPS signal (about 100 m) and the precision of sensors involved.

To correct this error, a procedure known as Map Matching is activated every 30 m. This involves correlating the route followed by the vehicle with the road network present in the map database. This correlation can be used to identify the vehicle's correct position on the ground.

The GPS data-based position correction procedure comes into play whenever new GPS data becomes available (about once per second under GPS coverage conditions). The data cannot, however, be called up more frequently than 10 times per second.

The system enters recorded differences between GPS reading and navigation estimation into a filter that estimates the GPS error variance. If variance drops below a preset threshold, the system corrects the position by making it tend gradually toward the position detected by the GPS. In other words, the more accurate the GPS readings, the more the system tends to use them without correction.

In the absence of satellite information, the navigation system uses information from the gyroscope and odometer for temporary data analysis.

The suggestions proffered by the navigation system do not relieve the driver of full responsibility for the consequences of all manoeuvres carried out in the traffic while driving the car and from respect for the highway code and other rules of the road. Responsability for road safety lies with the vehicle driver under all circumstances.

WARNINGS

GPS reception is difficult under trees, among high buildings, in multstorey car parks, in tunnels and in any place where satellite aerial reception may be hindered.

The GPS takes 15 minutes to activate if the vehicle battery is disconnected.

The GPS takes a few minutes to determine the vehicle's new position if the engine is turned off and the vehicle is moved with the system off (e.g. by means of a tow-truck).

The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects.

Instantaneous vehicle position is identified on the navigation system CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographic features of the area stored on the CD-ROM. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a few moments before the maps are displayed.

The navigation system takes about 50 km to self-regulate accurately from the first system start-up and when the tyres are changed.

In conditions where wheel grip is continuously bad (e.g. when sliding on ice), the system detects an inaccurate position temporarily.

The position is not recorded comprehensively during precision self-regulation.

It is possible to select several destinations that are managed in sequence as they are reached.

When a route is selected, the system generates all the information required to guide the user to the destination.

It computes effective distance to the destination and keeps it constantly updated; it explores the route ahead of the car to find the first cross-roads (intersection of at least 3 roads) where the user must make a Turn (i.e. follow a road that is not the natural continuation of the current road) and identifies the Manoeuvre (e.g. left turn) that the user must make; lastly, it computes the distance to the turn-off and updates the distance.

The system must take into account any deviations and check the vehicle is still on the correct route. If necessary it must carry out a Route Recalculation.

Fleet management function

This function is a brand new feature for the Connect system.

The user can send its position and additional information to a certain phone number by means of a text message.

This option allows users to manage their own vehicle fleet independently. Connect provides real-time information on vehicle position.

This option is available only for Connect versions with a GSM phone.

The fleet management function is suspended if the modem interface is active, because the GSM phone cannot be used simultaneously to send text messages and as a modem.

Operating procedure

When active, the "Fleet Management" service sends a text message [posizione + city name + street name + time + vehicle identification] to the fleet control centre phone number in accordance with a cyclic sequence set by the user using the GSM phone in Connect.

"Fleet management" service data are activated and entered by means of the "Fleet Setup" menu that can be activated from the "MAIN" page.

When a navigation CD is present, vehicle position is further processed by map matching to ensure correspondence with map co-ordinates in Connect.

Absence of the navigation CD does affect system operation.

The time transmitted is the time recorded by GPS.

The Connect system synchronises with the GPS time, when the GPS is visible to reconstruct a time base that can be used to define messages to be sent to the control centre.

The navigation system does not possess its own internal clock and cannot obtain time information from any other vehicle devices because the vehicle is not fitted with a telematic network.

Operating requirements

"Fleet management" function operation is dependent on the following conditions:

  • Function activated
  • Control centre phone number inserted
  • Vehicle identification [max. 20 alphanumerical characters] entered
  • Cyclic sequence setting
  • Connect on
  • SIM inserted and enabled
  • Sufficient credit
  • GSM coverage

Message format and content

The outgoing text message is in the following format: [position + city name + street name + time + vehicle identification]

"Position" is expressed by indicating latitude and longitude.

"City name" and "Street name" fields can be completed only with the navigation CD inserted.

Time is expressed in the following format: seconds;minutes;hours;day;date;'month;year.

The vehicle identification is the vehicle registration number.

Each field ends with the character '#'.

Each subfield ends with the character ;'.

The Latitude value is preceded by LT:.

The Longitude value is preceded by LG:.

What happens when a message cannot be sent

A text message cannot be sent if one of the following conditions arises at the time of transmission:

  • Connect off
  • SIM removed or not enabled
  • GSM signal inadequate

In this case, the system saves the last vehicle positions (up to a maximum of ten).

When normal service conditions are restored, the system sends inevitably delayed text messages containing saved positions.

If Connect is off (vehicle location not possible), the saved messages will contain an incorrect vehicle location (e.g. the first recorded upon reactivation).

Voice recognition function

The voice recognition function allows the user to interact with the Connect system by means of voice commands.

Various functions (navigation system, radio/CD, phone) can be managed according to the Connect configuration.

This function is designed to recognise the existence of words defined as "First Level" that enable a set of commands linked to a given environment. These commands remain available as long as the user pronounces another First Level word.

The command imparted with the First Level word determines access to a set of subordinate 2nd, 3rd and 4th level commands.

A set of service voice commands is also present that do not control a Connect function directly but are useful for managing user-system communication.

Operating Procedure

The Voice Recognition function operates in two ways:

  • Speaker Independent mode.
  • Speaker Dependent mode.

When in Speaker Independent mode, the Connect system analyses speech received from the microphone in accordance with a model independent of sex, tone of voice and user inflections. No training stage is required to interpret the commands.

The user presses the appropriate button to request interpretation of a voice command. The Connect continues the conversation and Guides the User to provide information required to carry out the requested service.

Speaker Dependent mode is available for voice interaction with the phone book and navigation system..

The User may, for example, associated each phone number in the Connect address book with a voice sample. The User may then ask Connect to make a phone call through recognition of a previously-stored voice sample.

In Speaker Dependent mode, Connect cannot be expected to recognise voice samples saved by a User other than the person speaking the commands.

Voice recognition is designed to communicate with the user is different languages.

Voice Memo

The voice recognition function allows the recording of voice messages known as Voice Memos.

The Voice Memo allows the user to record and play back a certain number of voice messages. The messages are recorded in sequence and the total space corresponds to 3 minutes (180 seconds).

The user-activated recording can last up to 180 seconds (depending on the available space) and ends automatically when this time is up.

The user can interrupt the recording manually in any case.

The Voice Memo can play back voice messages from the last message recorded followed by previous messages. Once everything in the memory has been played, the first message is played again. The voice memo can skip to the previous or next message.

The Voice Memo can clear the entire memory available for recording.

Address book

Connect contains two different address books: one for the phone and the other for the navigation system.

The purpose of both is to make it easier to enter data (a phone number or destination) required by the user without going through a long procedure each time.

This operation may be carried out once only and the result is saved in Connect and associated with a mnemonic. Then all you have to do is identify a saved option by selecting from a list or entering the mnemonic name.

Both address books are also stored in a back up memory (flash memory). This means that information stored persists even after the system has been turned on and off or after the battery has been disconnected.

PHONE BOOK

The following fields are present in the phone book:

  • name: mnemonic label for fast access to the list.
  • phone number: number used by Connect for calls.
  • origin: origin of item in phone book (Connect memory or SIM CARD).

Name and number may be entered by the user during creation of a new address book item. In this case, the origin field indicates that the item is stored permanently in the Connect internal address book.

Or Name and Number may be present on the SIM Card that the user has entered in the Connect SIM Reader. The System also displays this information as phone book items. After the Card has been inserted, the address book management module reads all the items on the Card and makes a copy by creating new temporary items if the name/number pair is not already present in the Connect address book. In this case, the origin field indicates that the item comes from the SIM CARD.

This item type is deleted from the address book when it is downloaded or the system is turned off.

The following phone book functions are available to the user:

  • enter new item
  • delete existing item
  • select item for phone call
  • modify name field or number field for an individual item.

All items on the SIM Card can also be copied permanently into the Connect address book (the origin field will thus be modified).

NAVIGATION ADDRESS BOOK

The following fields are present in the navigation phone book:

  • name: mnemonic label for fast access to the list.
  • description of geographical location defined by user: string consisting of town name/street name or name of associated POI...
  • co-ordinates: place co-ordinates (not made available to user and used internally for localisation or route calculation).

The user may enter the name during creation of a new address book item while description and co-ordinates are selected by accessing the map database.

The following phone book functions are available to the user:

  • selecting (via name) item for route calculation/vehicle localisation
  • modification of individual item name field.

Data Interface Function

Connect is designed to manage a DCE-type external hardware device (e.g. Computer, printer, ...)

The configuration normally used for computers, terminals, printers etc. is defined a DTE (Data Terminal Equipment) configuration.

The configuration normally used for modems is defined a DCE (Data Communications Equipment) configuration.

These different configurations define the type of signal that each device expects at each pin.

Any device may be configured as a DTE or DCE.

Connect acts as a DCE, the external device (typically a computer) acts as a DTE

A lead with a direct pin-to-pin connection is used as a connection device for this configuration.

Maximum transmission speed is as specified for the GSM Phone module, i.e. 9.6 kbps.

A serial line consisting of a lead with a direct pin-to-pin connection is used to connect the Connect system to the external device.

No dedicated connector is required. The pin-out is described in the paragraph on the pin-out.

Priority.

The serial interface used allows the system to detect data transmission/reception on the channel and thus establish access priority levels to the GSM transmission module.

Data interface priorities for Connect functions are described below.

TARGAsys SERVICES

The following message is displayed: Serial Connection Interrupted.

All data exchanged during the interrupted communication session on the serial line are lost.

At the end of the emergency call or activated service, the previously active communication session on the serial line is not automatically resumed.

Actiation, deactivation and use of the Data Interface

The DEFAULT status upon activation of Connect with key-ON or key-OFF is: Data communication on RS 232 line INACTIVE.

Note that engine start-up with a serial line GSM data communication session active causes the line to drop and loss of transmitted data. Conversely, engine shut-down does not affect the serial line GSM data communication session.

After engine shut-down, the Connect system remains active for 20 minutes unless the left encoder is pressed (immediate shut-down) or the GSM communication carries on.

If the GSM communication carries on to the end of the 20 minute period, a second 20 minute period will automatically start.

Note that extended serial line GSM data communication sessions (and also long phone calls) can drain the vehicle battery.

Speed alarm function

Operating principle

The Speed Alarm function issues an acoustic alarm and a visual alarm when vehicle speed exceeds a preset threshold "Vlim" (Speed limit).

The speed alarm and acoustic alarm function can be activated/deactivated from a dedicated menu.

The acoustic alarm takes the form of a set of tones.

The visual alarm takes the form of a screen message (1) "Attention: speed limit exceeded" that is displayed for 3s after the threshold has been exceeded. This visual alarm takes priority over every other display.

The alarm contains symbol (2) containing the set value.

Exceeding of Vlim triggers the acoustic and visual signals.

The acoustic signal remains active for a time established by the acoustic signal screen and the screen signal remains active for up to 3 s.

The signals are deactivated for V < Vlim-5 regardless of time elapsed

The user enters a numerical speed limit value by turning the encoder. The numbers change in steps = 5. Speed range [30-250]km/h, or [20-155] mph

The measurement unit applied to input numbers is as specified in the Setup menu in the "Distance Measurement" field (km or Miles).

If the speed alarm is deactivated (Alarm = inactive) and the speed limit is changed (e.g. from 130 to 190), it will activate automatically.

When the measurement units are changed from km to miles and viceversa, the number representing the speed threshold (Limit key) remains valid but takes the new measurement unit into account.

The set values are active only after confirming with the "OK" key..
